questions.question: Pulicat Lake, the second largest brackish water lagoon in India after Chilika, lies on the border of which two states?
options: D) Tamil Nadu and Andhra Pradesh
questions.explanation: Pulicat Lake, a brackish water lagoon and an important bird sanctuary, lies on the Coromandel Coast straddling the border of Tamil Nadu and Andhra Pradesh. It is the second largest such lagoon in India after Chilika Lake in Odisha.

questions.question: The Battle of Haldighati (1576), in which Maharana Pratap of Mewar fought the forces of the Mughal Empire, was fought against which Mughal general?
questions.explanation: The Battle of Haldighati was fought on 18 June 1576 between Maharana Pratap of Mewar and the Mughal forces led by Man Singh I of Amber, a general under Emperor Akbar. Though tactically indecisive, it became a symbol of Rajput resistance.

questions.question: Under which Article of the Indian Constitution can the President's Rule be imposed in a state if the government cannot function according to constitutional provisions?
questions.explanation: Article 356 empowers the President to impose President's Rule in a state if the President, on receipt of a report from the Governor or otherwise, is satisfied that a situation has arisen in which the governance of the state cannot be carried on in accordance with the provisions of the Constitution.

questions.question: Jog Falls, the second highest plunge waterfall in India, is formed by which river in Karnataka?
questions.explanation: Jog Falls, located in the Shivamogga district of Karnataka, is formed by the Sharavathi River plunging down a height of about 253 m. It is the second highest plunge waterfall in India after Nohkalikai Falls in Meghalaya.

questions.question: The Sambhar Salt Lake, India's largest inland salt lake and a key source of salt production, is located in which state?
questions.explanation: The Sambhar Salt Lake, located near Jaipur in Rajasthan, is India's largest inland salt lake. It has been a major source of salt production for centuries and is also a designated Ramsar wetland site.

questions.question: The Cripps Mission of 1942, which proposed Dominion Status for India after World War II, was sent by British Prime Minister Winston Churchill and led by which member of the British Cabinet?
questions.explanation: The Cripps Mission, sent to India in March 1942, was led by Sir Stafford Cripps, a senior member of the British War Cabinet. It proposed Dominion Status for India after the war but was rejected by both the Congress and the Muslim League.

questions.question: The Right to Education for children in the age group of 6-14 years as a Fundamental Right was added to the Indian Constitution by which Constitutional Amendment?
questions.explanation: The 86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002, inserted Article 21A, making the Right to Education a Fundamental Right for children aged 6-14 years. It also amended Article 45 and added a new Fundamental Duty under Article 51A(k).

questions.question: In October 2024, ISRO successfully conducted the first test flight of which abort demonstration mission, a key milestone in India's Gaganyaan human spaceflight programme?
questions.explanation: On 5 October 2024, ISRO successfully conducted the first test flight of the Gaganyaan crew abort system, designated TV-D1 (Test Vehicle Development Flight 1). The mission demonstrated the ability to safely abort the crew module in case of an emergency during launch.

questions.question: Who took over as the Chief of Army Staff (COAS) of the Indian Army in September 2024, succeeding General Manoj Pande?
questions.explanation: General Upendra Dwivedi took over as the 30th Chief of Army Staff on 30 September 2024, succeeding General Manoj Pande. Prior to this appointment, he served as the Vice Chief of Army Staff.

questions.question: The G20 Summit in 2025, under Brazil's presidency, will be held in which city?
questions.explanation: The 2025 G20 Summit, under Brazil's presidency, is scheduled to be held in Rio de Janeiro. Brazil assumed the G20 presidency on 1 December 2024, with a focus on global governance reform, sustainable development, and the fight against hunger.

questions.question: Group Captain Shubhanshu Shukla, selected for a private mission to the International Space Station in 2025, became the first Indian to go to the ISS under which programme?
questions.explanation: Group Captain Shubhanshu Shukla, an Indian Air Force test pilot and one of the four astronaut-designates for Gaganyaan, was selected to fly on Axiom Mission 4 (Ax-4) to the ISS, making him the first Indian to travel to the ISS on a private mission.

questions.question: Who took over as the Chief of Naval Staff (CNS) of the Indian Navy in April 2025, succeeding Admiral R. Hari Kumar?
questions.explanation: Admiral Dinesh K Tripathi took over as the Chief of Naval Staff on 30 April 2025, succeeding Admiral R. Hari Kumar. Prior to this, he served as the Vice Chief of Naval Staff and had also commanded the Eastern Naval Command.

questions.question: The 2024 Summer Olympics were held in Paris. Which Indian athlete won a bronze medal in the men's 5000m athletics event?
options: D) None — India won no athletics medals in 2024
questions.explanation: India did not win any athletics medals at the 2024 Paris Olympics. India's 6 medals came from shooting (3), wrestling (1), hockey (1), and tennis (1).

questions.question: India's first semiconductor fabrication plant, being set up by Tata Electronics in partnership with which company, received approval in 2024?
questions.explanation: Tata Electronics signed an agreement with Taiwan's Powerchip Semiconductor Manufacturing Corporation (PSMC) to set up India's first semiconductor fabrication plant in Dholera, Gujarat. The project received government approval in 2024 as part of India's semiconductor mission.

questions.question: In a certain code language, CAT is written as DCW (each letter is replaced by the letter whose position in the alphabet equals the original letter's position plus the letter's position in the word, counting from 1). How will INDIA be written in that code?
questions.explanation: Coding rule: new_letter_position = original_letter_position + position_in_word (1-indexed). INDIA: I(9)+1=10=J, N(14)+2=16=P, D(4)+3=7=G, I(9)+4=13=M, A(1)+5=6=F → JPGMF.

questions.question: A person walks 10 m north, then turns left and walks 5 m, then turns right and walks 15 m. In which direction is he facing now?
questions.explanation: The person walks 10 m north (facing north), turns left to face west and walks 5 m, then turns right to face north again and walks 15 m. He is facing north.

questions.question: Pointing to a woman, Raj said, 'She is the only daughter of my grandmother's only son.' How is the woman related to Raj?
questions.explanation: Raj's grandmother's only son is Raj's father. The woman is the only daughter of Raj's father, making her Raj's sister.

questions.question: If a clock shows 6:20 in a mirror, what is the actual time?
questions.explanation: The mirror image of a clock showing time T shows (12:00 - T). So if the mirror shows 6:20, the actual time is 12:00 - 6:20 = 5:40.

questions.question: Find the missing number in the series: 2, 5, 10, 17, 26, ?
questions.explanation: The pattern is n² + 1: 1²+1=2, 2²+1=5, 3²+1=10, 4²+1=17, 5²+1=26, 6²+1=37. The next term is 37.

questions.question: Stethoscope : Doctor :: Scalpel : ?
questions.explanation: A stethoscope is the primary diagnostic tool used by a doctor. Similarly, a scalpel is the primary cutting tool used by a surgeon.

questions.question: Find the next term of the letter series: A, C, F, J, O, ?
questions.explanation: The pattern of differences is +2, +3, +4, +5, +6: A+2=C, C+3=F, F+4=J, J+5=O, O+6=U. The next term is U.

questions.question: Find the odd one out: 8, 27, 64, 100, 125
questions.explanation: 8=2³, 27=3³, 64=4³, 125=5³ are all perfect cubes. 100 is not a perfect cube (it is 10²), making it the odd one out.

questions.question: What is 28% of 750?
If Rs 840 is divided between A and B in the ratio 5:2, how much does B get?
questions.explanation: Total parts = 5+2 = 7. B's share = (2/7) × 840 = Rs 240.

questions.question: The average of 6 numbers is 15. If one number is excluded, the average of the remaining 5 numbers becomes 13. What is the excluded number?
questions.explanation: Sum of 6 numbers = 6 × 15 = 90. Sum of 5 numbers = 5 × 13 = 65. Excluded number = 90 - 65 = 25.

questions.question: If 5 kg of rice costs Rs 225, what is the cost of 8 kg of rice at the same rate?
questions.explanation: Cost per kg = 225/5 = Rs 45. Cost of 8 kg = 45 × 8 = Rs 360.

questions.question: A shopkeeper marks his goods 30% above the cost price and then offers a discount of 20%. What is his net profit percentage?
A can complete a piece of work in 20 days. A and B together can complete the same work in 12 days. In how many days can B alone complete the work?
questions.explanation: A's 1 day work = 1/20. (A+B)'s 1 day work = 1/12. B's 1 day work = 1/12 - 1/20 = 5/60 - 3/60 = 2/60 = 1/30. B alone can complete the work in 30 days.

questions.question: A 100 m long train running at 36 km/h crosses a bridge in 30 seconds. What is the length of the bridge?
questions.explanation: Speed = 36 km/h = 36 × (5/18) = 10 m/s. Distance covered in 30 sec = 10 × 30 = 300 m. Bridge length = 300 - 100 = 200 m.

questions.question: A sum of money amounts to Rs 7,200 in 3 years and Rs 8,400 in 7 years at simple interest. What is the principal amount?
questions.explanation: Let P be the principal and r be the annual simple interest. P + 3r = 7200 and P + 7r = 8400. Subtracting: 4r = 1200, so r = 300. Then P = 7200 - 3(300) = 7200 - 900 = Rs 6,300.

questions.question: If x - y = 4 and xy = 45, what is the value of x² + y²?
The angles of a triangle are in the ratio 1:2:3. What is the measure of the largest angle?
questions.explanation: Sum of ratio parts = 1+2+3 = 6. Total = 180°. Largest angle = (3/6) × 180° = 90°.

questions.question: Find the next term in the series: 3, 7, 11, 15, 19, ?
questions.explanation: This is an arithmetic progression with common difference 4. The next term = 19 + 4 = 23.

questions.question: A cylindrical tank has a radius of 14 cm and a height of 15 cm. What is its volume? (Use π = 22/7)

The table below shows the monthly sales (in units) of a company for the first five months of 2025:
Month | Jan | Feb | Mar | Apr | May
Sales | 120 | 140 | 110 | 160 | 170
What is the average monthly sales over these five months?
The price of a shirt is first increased by 20% and then decreased by 15%. What is the net percentage change in the price?
questions.explanation: Net multiplier = 1.20 × 0.85 = 1.02, which represents a 2% increase over the original price.

questions.question: A bag contains 6 red, 4 blue and 5 green marbles. If two marbles are drawn at random without replacement, what is the probability that both are of the same colour?
questions.explanation: Total marbles = 15. Ways to draw 2 same colour = C(6,2) + C(4,2) + C(5,2) = 15 + 6 + 10 = 31. Total ways to draw 2 marbles = C(15,2) = 105. Probability = 31/105.

questions.question: If 1 January 2026 is a Thursday, what day of the week will 1 March 2026 be?
questions.explanation: From 1 Jan to 1 Mar = 31 (Jan) + 28 (Feb, 2026 is not a leap year) = 59 days. 59 days = 8 weeks + 3 days. Thursday + 3 days = Sunday.

questions.question:
Statements: All roses are flowers. All flowers are plants.
Conclusions: I. All roses are plants. II. All plants are roses.
Which conclusion(s) logically follow?
questions.explanation: Since all roses are flowers and all flowers are plants, by transitivity all roses are plants (I follows). However, we cannot conclude that all plants are roses (II does not follow).

questions.question: In a row of 40 students, Ankit is 15th from the left end. What is his position from the right end?
questions.explanation: Position from right = Total - Position from left + 1 = 40 - 15 + 1 = 26th.

questions.question: In a class of 50 students, 30 play cricket, 25 play football, and 10 play both. How many students play neither cricket nor football?
questions.explanation: Students playing at least one game = 30 + 25 - 10 = 45. Students playing neither = 50 - 45 = 5.

questions.question: What is the angle between the hour hand and the minute hand of a clock at 4:30?
questions.explanation: At 4:30, the hour hand is at 4.5 × 30° = 135° from 12 o'clock. The minute hand is at 180°. The angle between them = 180° - 135° = 45°.

questions.question: Six friends A, B, C, D, E, F sit in a row facing North. A is at the second position from the left end. C is immediately to the right of A. E is at the extreme right end. Who is immediately to the left of A?
questions.explanation: A is at position 2, C is at position 3, and E is at position 6. The person at position 1 (immediately to the left of A) could be any of B, D, or F. The given information does not determine who sits at position 1.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements and conclusions:
Statements: All dogs are mammals. Some mammals are cats. No cat is a bird.
Conclusions: I. Some dogs being cats is a possibility. II. No dog is a bird.
Which conclusion(s) logically follow from the statements?
questions.explanation: Since all dogs are mammals and some mammals are cats, it is possible that some dogs are cats (the overlap between mammals and cats could include dogs). So I follows. However, from 'All dogs are mammals' and 'No cat is a bird', we cannot establish any direct relationship between dogs and birds. II does not follow.

questions.question: Which blood group is known as the universal donor, whose red blood cells can be transfused to a person of any other ABO blood group in an emergency?
questions.explanation: Blood group O negative is the universal donor because its red blood cells have no A, B, or Rh antigens, making them compatible with all other blood groups in emergency transfusions.

questions.question: Which acid is present in the gastric juice of the human stomach, aiding in the digestion of proteins?
questions.explanation: Hydrochloric acid (HCl) is secreted by the parietal cells in the stomach lining. It creates an acidic environment (pH 1.5-3.5) that activates pepsinogen into pepsin, which digests proteins.

questions.question: Which physical quantity is measured in 'Ohms'?
questions.explanation: Ohm (Ω) is the SI unit of electrical resistance, named after Georg Simon Ohm. Electric current is measured in Amperes, power in Watts, and energy in Joules.

questions.question: Which cell organelle is known as the 'suicidal bag' of the cell because it contains hydrolytic enzymes that can break down the cell's own components if the organelle ruptures?
questions.explanation: Lysosomes are called the 'suicidal bag' of the cell because they contain powerful hydrolytic enzymes (proteases, lipases, nucleases) capable of digesting all biological macromolecules. If a lysosome ruptures, these enzymes can destroy the cell's own structures.

questions.question: As of 2025, India has the highest number of Ramsar wetland sites in South Asia. Which Indian state has the maximum number of Ramsar sites?
questions.explanation: As of 2025, Tamil Nadu has the highest number of Ramsar wetland sites in India, with over 15 designated sites including Point Calimere Wildlife Sanctuary, Pallikaranai Marsh, and Vettangudi Bird Sanctuary. India's total Ramsar sites crossed 85 in 2024-2025.

questions.question: The escape velocity from the surface of the Earth is approximately:
questions.explanation: The escape velocity from Earth's surface is approximately 11.2 km/s. This is the minimum speed an object must have to escape Earth's gravitational pull without further propulsion. (7.9 km/s is the orbital velocity.)
